# Phong N Do

> Phong N Do (also written Phong Do) is a math student at the University of
> California, Davis, an LLVM contributor, and a software engineer who builds
> developer tools: terminal multiplexers, diff reviewers, syntax
> highlighters, and agent harnesses, mostly in C++, Rust, Zig, and
> TypeScript. His site is https://phong.computer/.

## Now

- [LLVM](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pulls?q=is%3Apr+author%3Aphongndo): contributor to the LLVM compiler infrastructure. His patch "[IRNormalizer] Keep memory accesses in program order" was merged into LLVM (https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/237128), with more on the way.
- CloveGrowth: contract software engineer.
- CodeLab at UC Davis: software and infrastructure engineer, building with IBM.

## Projects

- [1harness](https://github.com/phongndo/1harness): one terminal UI for Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode, with threads that outlive the terminal. TypeScript.
- [Patch](https://github.com/phongndo/patch): native diff reviewer for macOS, Linux, and Windows. Zig.
- [Mark](https://github.com/phongndo/mark): fast, keyboard-first Git diff reviewer for the terminal. Rust.
- [hz](https://github.com/phongndo/hz): fast, isolated copy-on-write workspaces for parallel work by humans and agents. C++.
- [Syntaxmate](https://github.com/phongndo/syntaxmate): TextMate syntax highlighting library with bundled grammars and themes. Rust.
- [Frame](https://github.com/phongndo/frame): terminal multiplexer focused on performance and extensibility. C++.
- [Lemma](https://github.com/phongndo/lemma): agent harness for coding, writing, and research where every part, including the agent loop, is a replaceable plugin. TypeScript.
- [Petty](https://github.com/phongndo/petty): experimental Electron terminal multiplexer built on libghostty.

## About this site

- [Source](https://github.com/phongndo/portfolio): written in C++23 and compiled to WebAssembly. The background is a raymarched 3D slice of a 4D surface that blends Schoen's gyroid with Schwarz's P surface, rendered with WebGL2.
